description: Cross-driver corpus for personal-info preview masking. Every vector must produce the same `expected` in every driver's suite, unmodified. The policy below is a COPY of _shared/modules/personal_info/fields.toml [policy], carried here so a vector's expectation can be read without opening a second file; tools/test/test-personal-info-mask-corpus.cjs asserts the two agree, so a change to the TOML that is not reflected here fails rather than silently retargets every vector.

vectors.why: The grouping spaces survive and do not count toward head or tail — revealing 'FR' must mean two LETTERS, not a letter and a space. This is the vector a byte-slicing implementation gets wrong.
The same value without decoration. Head and tail land on the same characters as the spaced form, which is what makes the separator rule a display concern rather than an arithmetic one.

Eight characters, below min_length_to_reveal. Head 2 plus tail 4 would show six of the eight, which is not a mask. An implementation that applies the reveal unconditionally passes every other vector and fails this one.
Eleven is still below the threshold. The bound is on the value, not on the field.
The last four digits are how a card issuer asks you to identify a card, which is the whole reason the tail is larger than the head.
A French SSN's grouping is irregular, so the reveal cannot be computed from group boundaries — only from content position.
Explicitly exempt by the maintainer's decision. A vector whose expectation EQUALS its input is what proves the field table is being consulted at all rather than everything being masked.
Follows its sibling. Listed separately because a rule keyed on a name prefix would silently capture a future phone_number_work nobody classified.
Personal, but not a credential. Also short enough that a masking implementation ignoring the field table would return all bullets, which this catches.
A field nobody classified is hidden. The opposite default reveals whatever a future edit forgets to declare, which is the failure this whole file exists to prevent.
No field name means the value's provenance was lost on the way to the row, which is exactly when it must not be assumed public.
Nothing to mask and nothing to reveal. An implementation that pads to a minimum width would invent content.

Accented characters are two bytes in UTF-8. A byte-indexed implementation reveals half a character here and produces a string that is both wrong and unreadable — and the Lua drivers run on a LuaJIT with no utf8 library, so this is not hypothetical.
Twelve content characters is the boundary: min_length_to_reveal is inclusive, so this reveals. An off-by-one implementation hides it entirely and still passes every other vector.
Eleven hides. The pair with the vector above is what pins which side of the boundary is which.
